newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks close firm on foreign activity.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks close firm on foreign activity.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed firm on Monday with the index and turnover supported by foreign buying, brokers said.
The all share index closed 0.8 points higher at 621.3. Price gains and declines ran neck and neck at 18 each. Commercial Bank Ltd rose one rupee to 144, Hatton National Bank Ltd two rupees to 249.

"Despite the local government election, foreign buyers are willing to pay up for a substantial volume, especially if the company has seen good profits in 1996," said Shafi Waheed, a trader at CDIC Sasoon Cumberbatch.
Turnover was 22.57 million rupees on 433,171 shares. The main trades were 66,700 John Keells Holdings Ltd and 10,500 National Development Bank Ltd.
Brokers said there was selective buying despite investor caution ahead of the March 21 local government polls.

A parcel of 2.9 million Kegalle Plantations Ltd was on bid on an all-or-none basis at 19.50 rupees each. The seller was the Bank of Ceylon which underwrote the initial public offer. If a quantity is over five percent of a company's issued capital, the stock exchange requires the parcel to be introduced on an all-or-none basis and remain on bid for three days. --Prithi Kodagoda (941) 434319
